title: Chano Pozo at the Spanish Music Center session
summary: Chano taught Machito's percussionists their parts; Tito Puente learned in his band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: See, I'm glad you brought that up. That's where Chano Pozo (inaudible) used to try (inaudible). And I'm glad you brought that up because, before Chano got here, Machito Mangual and the whole band Majici used to tell McGuire, Miranda (inaudible) all there, (inaudible) and the conga, that they didn't know nothing about this, and Chano's ways (inaudible). They say, no, but (inaudible) Chano he's nothing like you're talking about. And people said Machito time would tell.
So when Chano got here, we went to recording A Bongo Session (inaudible) with Miguelito, for Sanger SMC or CMS.

But when we got to the studio, Carlos Mangual Vidal, everybody, Tito start playing, and Chano stop and said, is that 7" what (inaudible). And Chano said, no, no, no, no, wait a minute. (Inaudible), you do too-too-too-too-too-too, too-too, and do that from the beginning and (inaudible). Vidal, you do ka-ka, um-ka-ka, um-ka-ka, um-ka-ka, um-ka-ka. Gran, you pa-pa-pa-pa-pa. Miguelito know what he going to do (Inaudible), and I know what I'm going to do. Let's go one, two, three, four. Machito look at Mangual (Inaudible). See what happen to it?
These people thought that they already

discovered everything, that they knew. The last time I I couldn't find nobody (inaudible) to play a rhythm (inaudible). That little (inaudible) Machito's band in the beginning had to be taught to people. I don't have for three months. I've been (inaudible) for three months. He ain't got no idea what I went through. Now the scene is different. Everybody play. Or they do this, they think they play. (Inaudible). But there nobody play.

So when Chico Tiko left (inaudible) McGuire and some hinky-dink (inaudible). At least he got that thing, you know. He got that frame. (inaudible). The same thing that happen when Tito Puente I brought (inaudible) to the band. Chano (inaudible) got (inaudible) and got a hold of Tito Tico Puente. I said, teach him how to play the BAILA paya (phonetic), teach him how to do like this, to play the cowbell. (Inaudible) that kind of stuff.
Now, I hear people talk about the (inaudible). No, no. He learned that here, right in my band.
Sure, he got a natural ability to be able to (inaudible) that kind of stuff. Chano Pozo (inaudible) right in my band.
